dence of a role for oxidative stress in adult glioma. Vitamin C is a water soluble, well known scavenger of hydroxyl radicals that inhibits oxidative DNA lesions such as 8-hydroxydeoxyguanosine [27]. We observed an inverse association with adult glioma for vitamin C consumption, which is consistent with our previous results [2]. Regarding consumption of vitamin E, a lipid soluble free radical scavenger, we did not observe any statistically significantly differences between cases and controls,

although total dietary antioxidant index was statistically significantly inversely associated with glioma in this study. However, since results from other studies regarding the roles of vitamin's C and E with brain tumor risk are inconsistent 1,3,28-30 , the roles of antioxidant vitamins C & E may remain unclear.
